assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible-terminator sequencing-by-synthesis on clonally amplified clusters turned nucleotide chemistry into a readout that reshaped biology and medicine; a clear, original chemical invention with enormous lasting impact, including on how I measure and think about genome maintenance.
assessment.attribution: The Cambridge pair conceived and developed the sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry and single-molecule/cluster approach; Pascal Mayer (cluster amplification), Jingyue Ju (terminator chemistry) and Jonathan M. Rothberg (pyrosequencing, a distinct route) are also credited, so a three-person limit forces hard choices and I am not certain of the decisive split.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of use, independent platforms and clinical adoption; recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Allocation among Balasubramanian, Klenerman, Mayer, Ju and Rothberg is contested and I have not independently verified the patent and priority history.
Whether the committee treats this as chemistry or as a biology/medicine tool.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs that site-specifically install nonnatural amino acids rewrote a basic rule of protein chemistry and gave biologists a general tool to probe mechanism in proteins; original, conceptually clear and widely used.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo system in E. coli and then eukaryotes; Chin extended it to mammalian cells, multiple codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama made important contributions but the core trio seems defensible; some uncertainty in my memory on exact priority.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with 20+ years of independent reproduction and applications in therapeutics and imaging.
uncertainties: Relative weight of Chin versus Mehl and Yokoyama is uncertain.
Whether applications beyond tool use (e.g. therapeutic proteins) are sufficiently demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme behind biological nitrogen fixation; the atomic structure of the FeMo-cofactor and the mechanistic work on how it binds and reduces N2 address a central metalloenzyme chemistry question, which appeals to my interest in radical and metal-cofactor enzymology.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the crystallographic structures; Dean and Seefeldt contributed genetics and mechanism; Einsle resolved the central carbide at atomic resolution; Ribbe cofactor biosynthesis. The set is large and the decisive split is not clear to me.
assessment.maturity: Structure is well confirmed; the catalytic mechanism and substrate-binding site are still being refined, so recognition might be seen as partly early.
uncertainties: Exact site and mechanism of N2 reduction remain debated.
Attribution among five credited people is unresolved and I may misremember who made the decisive step.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry is the chemical foundation of automated oligonucleotide synthesis, supporting PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and nucleic-acid drugs; a beautifully clear chemical solution with exceptional breadth.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method and the solid-support route; Leroy Hood's contribution concerned automation instrumentation, which I see as supportive rather than decisive. I would credit Caruthers alone.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of independent validation, though that also means recognition is long overdue and a living laureate matters.
uncertainties: Contribution of earlier phosphotriester work (Khorana, Letsinger) may complicate credit.
Hood's role is not independently verified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base to another in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks, a deaminase-based chemical solution that is a general tool and already in clinical trials; important and original, building on a chemistry-minded design.
assessment.attribution: Liu conceived the editors; Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees who executed the cytosine and adenine editors, and Nishida/Kondo made a parallel cytidine editor. A single-laureate award to Liu is the cleanest, but the prior CRISPR prize narrows the framing.
assessment.maturity: Fairly young (2016-2017) with growing clinical evidence; confirmation is broad but long-term off-target and mutagenic effects, which are a genome-stability concern, are still being measured.
uncertainties: Off-target deamination and genome-wide mutagenesis need careful quantitative measurement.
Overlap with CRISPR prize and with prime editing (B030) may split recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mass-spectrometry proteomics made quantitative, proteome-scale measurement of proteins routine, and as a quantitative experimentalist I value the shift from qualitative to measured biology.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the most commonly central figures for methods, with Gygi, Hunt and Heck also strong; the field has many contributors, making a fair trio hard.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed, with ongoing improvements; some of the core ionization recognition was already given in 2002.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 chemistry prize for ESI/MALDI of biomolecules.
Many near-equivalent contributors make a three-person allocation arbitrary.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the chemistry that made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable, with demonstrated global impact in mRNA vaccines and siRNA drugs.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group developed the lipid chemistry and formulation; Hope and Madden were central early coworkers; MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer contributed as well. The 2023 Medicine prize went to mRNA modification, so credit here is for delivery chemistry.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at scale; mechanisms of endosomal escape and structure-activity are still partly empirical.
uncertainties: Attribution across academic and company contributors is unresolved and I have not verified it.
Partial overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that m6A is a reversible, enzymatically installed and erased mark, with FTO as an oxidative demethylase, turned RNA regulation into defined chemistry; broad biomedical relevance to cancer and development.
assessment.attribution: He identified FTO demethylation and the reader/writer framework; Jaffrey and Rechavi (with Dominissini) provided transcriptome-wide mapping. Several other labs contributed writers and readers, so allocation is not clear.
assessment.maturity: Field is about 15 years old; some mechanistic interpretations, including FTO substrate specificity and many functional claims, have been revised or contested, so maturity is less than the others.
uncertainties: Independent reproduction of mapping and of physiological demethylase roles is mixed.
Relative credit among He, Jaffrey, Rechavi, Dominissini and Jia is uncertain.
